B — Mapping: rulebook + CT context → circuit

Letter folder B_mapping/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/B_mapping/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

Turn a cited rulebook (published statistics only) plus A's context vector into a quantum circuit with no hand-written gates: a standalone Bayesian-network → circuit compiler (CPT → controlled rotations; one measurement = one joint sample). B-1: context selects the CPTs. B-2: site × phenotype drawn jointly in superposition (the novel contribution). B-5: QeMCMC tumor-in-anatomy energy sampler as a research arm. Quantum blur only together with its classical-blur baseline.

How to run (sim commands)

All commands run with cwd = reverse-engineering/ (conda base). Every quantum number is labelled simulated: ideal or simulated: Heron-class noise (FakeMarrakesh); hardware: null. Runs land in B_mapping/runs/<timestamp>-<tag>/ (gitignored).

python -m B_mapping.src.lidc_stats                              # data/lidc_counts.json (LIDC counts only)
python -m B_mapping.src.rulebook --write --joint --context free # data/rulebook_lung.json, class_prior.json
python -m B_mapping.src.compiler --check <rulebook.json>        # statevector vs exact joint, both control modes
python -m B_mapping.repro.borujeni --mode ideal|heron           # Borujeni 4-node repro (+ figure for heron)
python -m B_mapping.src.map --variant b1 --mode ideal|heron --site S001 [--sites F] [--certificate F] [--shots 4096]
python -m B_mapping.src.map --variant b2 --mode ideal|heron [--k-sites 8] [--multi-control mcry|ancilla]
python -m B_mapping.src.drift_report                            # B-1 x 3 classes + B-2, both modes, figure
python -m B_mapping.repro.layden                                # Layden gap scaling (ideal)
python -m B_mapping.src.qemcmc --tumor --mode ideal|heron [--patch 2,2,2|2,3,1]
python -m B_mapping.src.qemcmc_figure                           # figures/qemcmc_tumor_gap.png
python -m B_mapping.repro.wootton_blur                          # quantum blur vs Gaussian

Run a Python process alone or set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1: several concurrent BLAS-threaded jobs stalled the Layden run.

Claim level and honesty notes

  • B-1: claim level L0 (provenance only: a certified sample of a classical distribution). The classical ancestral sampler draws the same distribution with lower error at the same shot count.
  • B-2: claim level L0. The joint site × phenotype draw is a lookup table classically; no interference claim, no entanglement witness (WitnessRecord is D's).
  • QeMCMC: no claim level. A correct sampler with quantum proposals; any speedup is ideal-simulation only (Layden k_quantum 0.250 vs k_local 1.017, simulated: ideal) and the noisy proposal is asymmetric (0.135).
  • Quantum blur: none. Equivalent to a Gaussian where it blurs; rejected.
  • Belief-propagation simulability number for the B circuits: pending D #9 (gate counts are recorded in each run's drift.json).
  • Context tilts and the placement prior are marked (verify) in the rulebook sources: the cited papers are not in ../papers/.
  • The stub anatomy_masks give an almost flat tumor energy landscape (h ≈ −0.1 everywhere); the QeMCMC adaptation needs A's real masks to say more.
  • Real A output and the real C certificate are not wired in here (INT).

Pipeline readiness

Prototype

Ideal draws match the classical sampler (joint TVD 0.018–0.039), but under Heron-class noise the draw is noise-dominated (TVD 0.571–0.737, 33–59 % invalid shots at depth 5 862–31 965). The chain asks for B-2 at K = 8 in Heron mode, a setting that has only run ideal (depth 106 531, 38 123 CZ), so its cost and validity are unknown. The honesty gate is still open: B's circuits have no BP simulability number, because D's BP adversary cannot read a B circuit (probe runs/20261029-185947-probe-gaps: bp --circuit missing). All map flags the chain uses exist.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [B01] Low–Yoder–Chuang: write a Bayesian network (a chain of conditional probabilities) as a quantum circuit, so one measurement returns one joint sample, with a possible quadratic speedup for inference.
  • [B09] / [B10] Borujeni: a practical recipe for such circuits, and its accuracy on IBM hardware.
  • [B11] Layden, [B12] Ferguson–Wallden: quantum-enhanced Markov-chain Monte Carlo, with quantum proposals that can mix faster on rugged energy landscapes, extended to problems larger than the device.
  • [B04] / [B05] Wootton: quantum procedural generation and "quantum blur" for images.

Why it matters: a rulebook made only of published statistics, compiled without hand-written gates, makes every tumour property traceable to a citation.

2. Contribution

  • A standalone BN → circuit compiler: Borujeni marginal RMSPE 0.36 % (mcry) / 0.18 % (ancilla) against the paper's 0.1 %, and marginals within ±0.01 of Netica. evidence-based
  • QeMCMC reproduced: k_quantum / k_local / k_uniform = 0.250 / 1.017 / 0.939 against 0.264 / 0.94 / 0.948 (simulated: ideal). evidence-based
  • B-2, a joint site × phenotype draw: placement and tumour type drawn together in one quantum job. evidence-based
  • An honest drift table: ideal circuits equal the classical sampler (TVD 0.018–0.039); Heron-class noise does not (0.571–0.737). Quantum blur is rejected (correlation 0.967 / 0.993 with a Gaussian). evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: cohorts whose tumour mix (type, size, margin, location) follows a cited rulebook exactly, with every draw traceable. That turns detector testing into a controlled experiment: "how does sensitivity change for 6 mm ground-glass nodules at the pleura?" extrapolation The quantum circuit provides provenance (claim level L0). It does not provide better tumours: the classical sampler draws the same distribution with lower error today. evidence-based

4. Beyond lungs

  • Any disease with published statistics. Liver, breast (procedural breast phantoms [H12]) and brain lesions can be rulebooks too: the compiler is organ-agnostic. extrapolation
  • Comprehensive medicine. BN nodes can encode comorbidities, risk factors or drug-response categories. A rulebook is then machine-readable clinical knowledge that a cohort generator samples from. extrapolation
  • Treatment and drug response. Conditional tables such as "response | phenotype, dose" would let virtual cohorts carry an outcome label. speculative

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative B is the twin's prior-knowledge layer. Path: (1) a tumour-phenotype rulebook (now) → (2) a patient-level network (age, smoking, genetics → risk → phenotype) → (3) conditioning on the patient's own measurements, so the twin samples only futures consistent with them → (4) quantum sampling of very large joint distributions, which pays off only when the circuits are deep and error-corrected [B01]. Step 4 is the only quantum-dependent step.

6. Predictions

5 years Assumptions: Heron-class noisy devices; noise as in FakeMarrakesh; the classical ancestral sampler stays the baseline.

  • At chain depth (5 862–31 965) Heron-class draws are noise-dominated (TVD 0.57–0.74, 33–59 % invalid shots). evidence-based
  • Useful near-term setups are small rulebooks, shallower compilations and K ≤ 4 sites, or an ideal draw stamped with a hardware certificate. extrapolation
  • B's BP simulability number (D #9) shows these circuits are classically easy at their width. extrapolation

10 years Assumptions: devices that run 10⁴–10⁵ two-qubit gates with error mitigation (utility-scale results exist before fault tolerance [H11]).

  • B-2 at K = 8–16 sites runs at chain depth with drift close to the classical sampler. extrapolation
  • QeMCMC proposals run on real-anatomy energy landscapes. Any speedup is unproven: today it exists in ideal simulation only. extrapolation

15 years Assumptions: fault-tolerant hardware with deep, error-corrected circuits.

  • speculative Amplitude-amplified inference over large networks [B01] could estimate rare-event probabilities (rare phenotype × location combinations) with quadratically fewer samples. This is a claim-level-L3 capability and the first point where B's quantum path could beat its classical baseline.

Contract change requests

CCR-B1: rulebook, class prior slot.

  • Need: the placement-class prior P(free, juxtavascular, juxtapleural) belongs to the rulebook (A emits equal counts per class).
  • Request: an optional top-level params object (or prior field) in rulebook; nodes and top level are additionalProperties: false / unevaluatedProperties: false today.
  • Local workaround: sidecar data/class_prior.json, read by joint.py.

CCR-B2: compiled_circuit, logical-to-physical layout and ancillas.

  • Need: record the logical qubit order (clbit i = logical qubit i, node order, little-endian) and which physical qubits are ancillas.
  • Request: an optional extra object on compiled_circuit.
  • Local workaround: qubit_map holds the physical qubit whose measurement feeds each node's clbits (matches $n in the QASM); ancillas are an extra key ancilla (final layout); the logical order is documented here. No information is lost for decoding because decoding uses the compiler's own maps.
